title: Boolean duality preserves failure probability
statement: Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{\\pm1\\}$ be a Boolean function, let $\\delta\\in\\mathbb R$, and let $k$ be a natural number. The coordinate-switching failure probability at parameter $\\delta$ and threshold $k$ is unchanged when $f$ is replaced by its Boolean dual, the function $x\\mapsto -f(-x)$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the n-dimensional sign cube
